This file contains all the code I used to query and update the CLEAR lab air quality database during my role as CLEAR lab Database Manager during the 2026-2027 school year. The role commenced on September 21, 2026. 

```{r, eval=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(lubridate)
library(PurpleAirAPI)
library(DBI)
library(odbc)
library(PurpleAir)


con = dbConnect(
  odbc(),
  Driver = "/opt/homebrew/lib/libmsodbcsql.18.dylib",
  Server = "resdbsprdhs02.adms.luc.edu",
  Database = "clearlab_purpleair",
  UID = Sys.getenv("DB_USERNAME"),
  PWD = Sys.getenv("DB_PASSWORD"),
  Encrypt = "yes",
  TrustServerCertificate = "yes"
)


```



#September 2026


### 9/21/26: 

After orienting a fellow lab member with the updated database schema and the high level workflow of the R scripts used to update the Purpleair, Clarity, and Airgradient tables, the very first change I made was to update the sensor_activity_status column for each sensor company, so that it determined whether a sensor was active based on a period of time relative to the current date instead of relative to a fixed date.

```{r, eval=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

dbExecute(con, "ALTER TABLE Purpleair_sensor_information 
          DROP COLUMN sensor_activity_status")
dbExecute(con, "ALTER TABLE Purpleair_sensor_information 
          ADD sensor_activity_status VARCHAR(50)")

for (i in sensor_information$sensor_index) {

  query <- "
UPDATE Purpleair_sensor_information
SET sensor_activity_status =
    CASE
      WHEN CAST(last_seen AS date) >= DATEADD(day, -30, CAST(GETDATE() AS DATE))
        THEN 'Active'
      ELSE 'Inactive'
    END
  WHERE sensor_index = ?"
  
  dbExecute(con, query, params = list(i))
}

```

At the request of my supervisor, who was my mentor during my Summer 2026 USRE project, I investigated reported sparseness in Purpleair sensors' historical data during 2026. I did this by seeing which sensors pulled data during 2025 and which sensors pulled data during 2026, and then comparing those two sets of sensors. 

```{r, eval=FALSE, echo=FALSE}


PurpleAir_2026_data<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM Purpleair_air_history WHERE time_stamp > '2026-01-01 00:00:00'")


Purpleair_sensors_2025<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM Purpleair_air_history WHERE time_stamp BETWEEN '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND '2026-01-01 00:00:00'")

#I then used the following (AI generated) code to get a list of sensors that a) were in the 2025 data but not the 2026 data, and b) were in the 2026 data but not the 2025 data. It is simply performing set comparisons between the two vectors of sensor indices. 

unique(PurpleAir_2026_data$sensor_index[
  !PurpleAir_2026_data$sensor_index %in% Purpleair_sensors_2025$sensor_index 
])

unique(Purpleair_sensors_2025$sensor_index[
  !Purpleair_sensors_2025$sensor_index %in% PurpleAir_2026_data$sensor_index 
])

#At the time I ran this code on 9/21, the first set comparison printed nothing, indicating that all the sensors in the 2026 data were in the 2025 data. The second set comparison, however, revealed that 54 of the sensors in the 2025 data were not in the 2026 data. I wrote this list of sensors, along with the most recent timestamp of each sensor in the historical data, to a csv file to share with my supervisor.

Purpleair_air_history<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT sensor_index, time_stamp FROM Purpleair_air_history")
max_timestamp_by_index<-Purpleair_air_history%>%
filter(sensor_index %in% c(151042, 151050, 251599, 233117, 220537, 220553, 220531, 220591, 220577, 221165, 220613, 220223, 220177,220209,220191, 220583, 220261, 137618, 193689, 193669, 220579, 220521, 193661, 179769, 244039, 244063, 95075, 244057, 244083, 36281, 180725, 265767,  43955, 45359, 51933, 96079, 96933, 124513, 124649, 124685, 124715, 124737, 133664, 137622, 144504, 147893, 148029, 150066, 171015, 169187, 185239, 186099, 187615, 203303))%>%
group_by(sensor_index)%>%
summarize(max_timestamp=max(time_stamp))

write.csv(max_timestamp_by_index, "2025_PurpleAir_sensors_not_in_2026_data", row.names = FALSE)

```

My supervisor then gave me a list of 4 Loyola owned Purpleair sensors that were not in the database, for which I downloaded metadata and historical data and updated the respective tables. 

```{r, eval=FALSE}

fields=c("date_created", "last_seen", "name", "location_type", "model", "hardware", "latitude", "longitude", "private")
newdata <- getPurpleairSensors_debugged(apiReadKey=api_key, fields=fields) 

#This was a version of the getPurpleairSensors function, which I had previously edited to pull additional metadata fields in order to match the schema of the Purpleair_sensor_information table (see the Week 2 section of my Summer_2026_Air_Quality_Research Github repository for details about this).

newdata_new_sensors<-newdata%>%

newdata_new_sensors

```

Metadata for only 3 of the desired sensor indices was pulled from the API (the index 304778 was not). Regardless, I appended the metadata I could retrieve to the Purpleair_sensor_information table.

```{r, eval=FALSE }

dbWriteTable(
  con,
  name="Purpleair_sensor_information",
  value=newdata_new_sensors, 
  append=TRUE,
  row.names=FALSE)

#I then attempted to download historical data for all four sensors in my supervisor's list.

api_key<-Sys.getenv("API_KEY")
sensor_index <- c("309628", "309644", "304778", "304768")

start_date <- "2024-01-01"
end_date   <- "2026-09-24"
average <- "60"  # hourly
fields <- c(
  "humidity",
  "temperature",
  "pressure",
  "pm2.5_cf_1_a",
  "pm2.5_cf_1_b",
  "rssi"
)

historical_data <- getSensorHistory(
  sensorIndex = sensor_index,
  apiReadKey  = api_key,
  startDate   = start_date,
  endDate     = end_date,
  average     = average,
  fields      = fields
)

table(historical_data$sensor_index)


```


Not only did the API's historical data not contain readings for all 4 sensors, but the 3 sensors that did have historical readings (304768, 304778, and 309644) were a different set of 3 than the sensors that had metadata (304768, 309628,and 309644). This means that only 2 of the 4 sensors had both historical data and metadata, and of those 2, one had only 30 historical observations. Regardless, I updated the database with all the historical data  available at the time.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

dbWriteTable(con,
             name="Purpleair_air_history",
             value=historical_data, 
             append=TRUE,
             row.names=FALSE)

```


### 9/25/26:

I downloaded historical Airgradient sensor data for 7/5/26-7/20/26 (the week with the worst air quality of the summer in the Chicago area and the week prior to that), in order to provide the data to two graduate students working in the lab, so they could use it for a co-location study.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

Sys.getenv("LUC_CLEAR_AIRGRADIENT_API_KEY")

Airgradient_sensor_information<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM Airgradient_sensor_information")

library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)
token=Sys.getenv("LUC_CLEAR_AIRGRADIENT_API_KEY")
location_ids <- c("190848", "190849", "190850", "190851", "190852", "190853", "190854", "190855", "190856", "190857", "190858", "190859", "190860", "190861", "190862", "190863", "190864")

all_data <- list()

for (id in location_ids){
  url <- paste0("https://api.airgradient.com/public/api/v1/locations/", id, "/measures/past")
  
  response <- GET(
    url,
    query = list(
      token = token,
      from = "2026-07-05",
      to   = "2026-07-12")
  )
  
  if (status_code(response) != 200) {
    warning("Request failed for sensor ", id, " with status ", status_code(response))
    next
  }
  
  json_text <- content(response, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8")
  df <- fromJSON(json_text, flatten = TRUE)
  
  df$location_id <- id
  
  all_data[[id]] <- df
}

final_df_1 <- bind_rows(all_data)

#Owing to the fact that Airgradient's API only allows a date range up to a week long for historical data requests, I had to perform two requests and then combine the resulting dataframes together.

all_data_2 <- list()

for (id in location_ids){
  url <- paste0("https://api.airgradient.com/public/api/v1/locations/", id, "/measures/past")
  
  response <- GET(
    url,
    query = list(
      token = token,
      from = "2026-07-13",
      to   = "2026-07-20")
  )
  
  if (status_code(response) != 200) {
    warning("Request failed for sensor ", id, " with status ", status_code(response))
    next
  }
  
  json_text <- content(response, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8")
  df <- fromJSON(json_text, flatten = TRUE)
  
  df$location_id <- id
  
  all_data_2[[id]] <- df
}

final_df_2 <- bind_rows(all_data_2)

July_5_thru_20_Airgradient_data<-bind_rows(final_df_1, final_df_2)[ ,-27] #The 27th column is simply a repeat of the locationID field

July_5_thru_20_Airgradient_Data<-write.csv(July_5_thru_20_Airgradient_data, file="July_5_thru_20_Airgradient_Data", row.names=FALSE)

```

### 10/12/26: downloading PurpleAir data based on a list of sensor indices Dr. Whalen sent me (after updating all three databases with their respective update scripts). Some of these sensors are in the city of Chicago proper, while others are outside the city but within Cook County. 

### Dr. Whalen wanted me to add all the sensors to the metadata table, but to only add historical data from the Chicago city sensors (this means marking the Cook County sensors as inactive/not pulling in Chicago in the metadata table).

```{r, eval=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
New_sensors_to_add<-read_csv("~/Desktop/CLEAR lab database mangement 26-27/CLEAR_lab_database_work/purple air sensors.csv")
sensor_indices<-c()
New_sensors_to_add<-New_sensors_to_add%>%
filter(sensor_index != 'NA')
for (i in New_sensors_to_add$sensor_index){
  sensor_indices<-c(sensor_indices, i)}


fields=c("date_created", "last_seen", "name", "location_type", "model", "hardware", "latitude", "longitude", "private")
api_key<-Sys.getenv("PURPLE_AIR_API_KEY")
new_metadata<-getPurpleairSensors_debugged(apiReadKey = api_key, fields=fields)
new_metadata<-new_metadata%>%
filter(sensor_index %in% sensor_indices)
Unknown_sensor<-New_sensors_to_add%>%
filter(sensor_index !in c(new_metadata$sensor_index))

new_sensor_indices_retrieved<-new_metadata$sensor_index
print(New_sensors_to_add$sensor_index[which(!(New_sensors_to_add$sensor_index %in% new_sensor_indices_retrieved))])
#The index 171443 was not in the downloaded metadata. I will try downloading this sensor's metadata separately.

sensor_171443_metadata<-new_metadata%>%
filter(sensor_index==171443)
nrow(sensor_171443_metadata)
#This did not return any metadata for the sensor. I will add the other 41 sensors to the database and discuss this pesky individual with Dr. Whalen.

colnames(new_metadata)

#Moving the 'private' column after the 'longitude' column to match the structure of the database (AI helped me here; I had not seen this method before)

library(dplyr)
new_metadata <- new_metadata %>% relocate(private, .after = longitude)

new_metadata<-new_metadata%>%
mutate(temp_date_column=as.Date(last_seen))%>%
mutate(sensor_activity_status=case_when(
  temp_date_column>=Sys.Date()-30 ~ "Active",

#We want the metadata for all these sensors, but we don't want the historical data for the non Chicago sensors.
Non_Chicago_sensors<-New_sensors_to_add%>%
filter(Location != "Chicago")%>%
select(sensor_index)
Non_Chicago_sensor_indices<-Non_Chicago_sensors$sensor_index

#This means I need to set the sensor_activity_status column to Inactive for the sensor indices from the Cook County Suburbs (all of the sensors are currently Active based on their last_seen date).

new_metadata<-new_metadata%>%
left_join(New_sensors_to_add, by=c("sensor_index"="sensor_index"))

  Location=="Chicago" ~ "Active",

select(sensor_index, date_created, last_seen, name.y, location_type, model, hardware, latitude.y, longitude.y, private, sensor_activity_status)

colnames(New_metadata)[9]="longitude"

dbWriteTable(

c<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM Purpleair_sensor_information")
```

### 10/18/26: investigating the number of sensors reporting throughout 2026

I investigating the trend in the number of sensors reporting data on each day throughout the year 2026 as a time series.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

Purpleair_2026_historical_data<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM Purpleair_air_history WHERE time_stamp >= '2026-01-01 00:00:00'")

Purpleair_2026_investigation_data<-Purpleair_2026_historical_data%>%
mutate(Date=as.Date(time_stamp))%>%
arrange(Date)

Date_list<-as.Date(character())
Reporting_sensors_list<-c()

for(i in unique(Purpleair_2026_investigation_data$Date)){
  new_data<-Purpleair_2026_investigation_data%>%
  filter(Date==i)
  Date_list<-c(Date_list, i)
  print(i)
  Num_distinct_reporting_sensors<-length(unique(new_data$sensor_index))
  Reporting_sensors_list<-c(Reporting_sensors_list, Num_distinct_reporting_sensors)}

dates_targeted_inquiry<-as.Date(character())
for (i in Date_list){
  index=which(Date_list==i)
  if (Reporting_sensors_list[index] <= 5){
    dates_targeted_inquiry<-c(dates_targeted_inquiry, Date_list[index])}
}

ts_data_frame<-data.frame(Date=Date_list, Num_sensors_reporting=Reporting_sensors_list)

#Creating the time series

library(plotly)
Purpleair_sensors_reporting<-plot_ly(data=ts_data_frame, x=~Date, y=~Num_sensors_reporting, type="scatter", mode="lines", col="blue")%>%
layout(yaxis=list(range=c(0,80)))
Purpleair_sensors_reporting

```

When I initially generated this plot, the line was at 1-3 sensors for the entire period from January 1 to June 1. I suspect this is because I initially set the sensor_activity_status column based on a static 30 day threshold and only recently (on 9/21/26) changed the column definition to a moving 30 day threshold relative to the current date. 

I then backfilled the sensor data that was unaccounted for prior to me changing the column definition (going up to the current date just to be safe).

```{r, eval=FALSE}


vec<-unique(Purpleair_2026_historical_data$sensor_index)

sensor_index <- vec

start_date <- "2026-01-01"
end_date   <- "2026-10-18"
average <- "60"  
fields <- c(
  "humidity",
  "temperature",
  "pressure",
  "pm2.5_cf_1_a",
  "pm2.5_cf_1_b",
  "rssi"
)

historical_data <- getSensorHistory(
  sensorIndex = sensor_index,
  apiReadKey  = api_key,
  startDate   = start_date,
  endDate     = end_date,
  average     = average,
  fields      = fields
)

nrow(historical_data)

table(historical_data$sensor_index)
colnames(historical_data)
historical_data<-historical_data%>%
mutate(pm_2p5_diff=pm2.5_cf_1_a-pm2.5_cf_1_b)%>%
mutate(pm2p5_cf_1_a=pm2.5_cf_1_a, pm2p5_cf_1_b=pm2.5_cf_1_b)

library(dplyr)
historical_data<-historical_data %>% 
relocate(sensor_index, .before = time_stamp)%>%
relocate(humidity, .before = rssi)%>%
relocate(pm_2p5_diff, .after=pm2p5_cf_1_b)%>%
relocate(rssi, .before=pm_2p5_diff)%>%
  
historical_data<-historical_data%>%
select(-pm2.5_cf_1_a, -pm2.5_cf_1_b)
colnames(historical_data)[9]="pm2p5_diff"


```

I then cleaned the duplicates out of Purpleair_air_history.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

duplicate_historical_records<- dbGetQuery(con, 
                                "SELECT
    sensor_index, time_stamp, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM Purpleair_air_history
GROUP BY sensor_index, time_stamp
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1")

nrow(duplicate_historical_records)

dbExecute(con, "
WITH duplicates AS (
    SELECT *,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY sensor_index, time_stamp
               ORDER BY sensor_index, time_stamp) 
               AS rn
    FROM Purpleair_air_history)
DELETE FROM duplicates
WHERE rn > 1")

```

This removed 240,242 duplicate records, which is far fewer than the number of records added to the database.



# November 2026:



11/9/26: Revising the air_history table of each sensor company to include a pull_id column, like the trigger_pulls tables. When creating an ER diagram of the database using dBeaver, I realized that I could only make connections between the air_history tables and the sensor_information tables because these tables share a sensor_index field. The pull_id field in the trigger_pulls tables is not shared with any other table, preventing me from making connections to the trigger_pulls tables.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

dbExecute(con, "ALTER TABLE Purpleair_air_history ADD pull_id INT") #This ensures that all current rows in the table recieve a NULL value for the pull_id column, but subsequent rows appended later will have valid integer values (guidance from Microsoft Learn)

a<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM Purpleair_trigger_pulls")

b<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT pull_id FROM Purpleair_air_history")
head(b, 10)

```

To reflect these changes when I run the PurpleAir_24_hour update script, I will modify the update script so that it does not append the new historical data to the database until the pull_id value from the new row of trigger_pulls is supplied to all the values of the new historical dataframe. Specifically, I changed the historical data/metadata about historical pull part of the update script from this:


```{r, eval=FALSE}

### 4. Fetch and Process Historical Data

#Wrap historical steps in an IF block to prevent errors if 0 sensors need updates

if (length(updated_sensors) > 0) { 
  
  current_time <- Sys.time()
  time_query <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT MAX(time_stamp) AS time_stamp FROM Purpleair_air_history")
  initial_time<-time_query$time_stamp
  
  start_date_str <- format(initial_time,  format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")
  end_date_str   <- format(current_time, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")
  
  update_raw<-NULL
  
  tryCatch({update_raw = getSensorHistory(
    sensorIndex = updated_sensors, 
    apiReadKey=Purpleair_api_key,
    startDate=start_date_str,
    endDate=end_date_str,
    average='0', 
    fields=c('humidity', 'temperature', 'pressure', 'pm2.5_cf_1_a', 'pm2.5_cf_1_b', 'rssi')
  )
  
  cat(
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    "- Pulled previous 24 hours of historical data\n"
  )}, error= function(e) {
    cat(format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "- ERROR: Purpleair API history pull failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  })
  
  if (!is.null(update_raw) && nrow(update_raw) > 0) {
  
  update_clean = update_raw %>% 
    mutate(
      pm2p5_cf_1_a = `pm2.5_cf_1_a`,
      pm2p5_cf_1_b = `pm2.5_cf_1_b`,
      pm2p5_diff   = pm2p5_cf_1_a - pm2p5_cf_1_b)%>%
    select(sensor_index, time_stamp, humidity, temperature, pressure,
           pm2p5_cf_1_a = `pm2.5_cf_1_a`, pm2p5_cf_1_b = `pm2.5_cf_1_b`, rssi, pm2p5_diff)
  
  cat(
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    "- Processed and cleaned historical data\n"
  )
  
  
  dbWriteTable(conn = con,
               name = 'Purpleair_air_history',
               value = update_clean,
               append = TRUE,
               row.names = FALSE)
  
  cat(
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    "- Appended historical data to air_history\n"
  )
  
  sensor_list_string <- paste(sensors_pulled_log, collapse = ", ")
  
###5. Add metadata about the new historical pulls to the trigger_pulls table
  
  trigger_log_df <- data.frame(
    pull_timestamp    = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    rows_inserted     = as.integer(nrow(update_clean)),
    sensors_processed = sensor_list_string,
    stringsAsFactors  = FALSE
  )
  
  dbWriteTable(conn=con, name='Purpleair_trigger_pulls', value=trigger_log_df, append=TRUE, row.names=FALSE)
  
  cat(
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    "- Appended historical pull metadata to trigger_pulls table\n"
  )
  
} else { cat(format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "- No sensors required historical updates.\n") }
}

```


to this:


```{r, eval=FALSE}

if (length(updated_sensors) > 0) { 
  
  current_time <- Sys.time()
  time_query <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT MAX(time_stamp) AS time_stamp FROM Purpleair_air_history")
  initial_time<-time_query$time_stamp
  
  start_date_str <- format(initial_time,  format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")
  end_date_str   <- format(current_time, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")
  
  update_raw<-NULL
  
  tryCatch({update_raw = getSensorHistory(
    sensorIndex = updated_sensors, 
    apiReadKey=Purpleair_api_key,
    startDate=start_date_str,
    endDate=end_date_str,
    average='0', 
    fields=c('humidity', 'temperature', 'pressure', 'pm2.5_cf_1_a', 'pm2.5_cf_1_b', 'rssi')
  )
  
  cat(
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    "- Pulled previous 24 hours of historical data\n"
  )}, error= function(e) {
    cat(format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "- ERROR: Purpleair API history pull failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  })
  
  if (!is.null(update_raw) && nrow(update_raw) > 0) {
  
  update_clean = update_raw %>% 
    mutate(
      pm2p5_cf_1_a = `pm2.5_cf_1_a`,
      pm2p5_cf_1_b = `pm2.5_cf_1_b`,
      pm2p5_diff   = pm2p5_cf_1_a - pm2p5_cf_1_b)%>%
    select(sensor_index, time_stamp, humidity, temperature, pressure,
           pm2p5_cf_1_a = `pm2.5_cf_1_a`, pm2p5_cf_1_b = `pm2.5_cf_1_b`, rssi, pm2p5_diff)
  
  cat(
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    "- Processed and cleaned historical data\n"
  )
  
 #Notice that I do not append the new historical data to Purpleair_air_history yet
  
  sensor_list_string <- paste(sensors_pulled_log, collapse = ", ")
  
###5. Add metadata about the new historical pulls to the trigger_pulls table
  
  trigger_log_df <- data.frame(
    pull_timestamp    = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    rows_inserted     = as.integer(nrow(update_clean)),
    sensors_processed = sensor_list_string,
    stringsAsFactors  = FALSE
  )
  
  dbWriteTable(conn=con, name='Purpleair_trigger_pulls', value=trigger_log_df, append=TRUE, row.names=FALSE)
  
    cat(
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    "- Appended historical pull metadata to trigger_pulls table\n"
  )

  Max_pull_timestamp<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT MAX(pull_timestamp) FROM Purpleair_trigger_pulls")
  Max_pull_time_stamp<-ymd_hms(Max_pull_timestamp[1,1])
  New_pull_id<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT pull_id FROM Purpleair_trigger_pulls WHERE pull_timestamp=?", params=list(Max_pull_time_stamp))
New_pull_id_integer=as.numeric(New_pull_id[1,1])
  
  ###The new part: Querying the most recent value of pull_id from PurpleAir_trigger_pulls (the value corresponding to the most recent row of historical update metadata)
  
  update_clean_with_pull_id<-update_clean%>%
    mutate(pull_id=rep(New_pull_id_integer, nrow(update_clean))) #Populating a pull_id column for the new historical dataframe containing the new value of pull_id (a one to many relationship exists between the pull_id in trigger_pulls and the pull_id in air_history)
  
    dbWriteTable(conn = con,
               name = 'Purpleair_air_history',
               value = update_clean_with_pull_id,
               append = TRUE,
               row.names = FALSE) 
    
    #I wait to append the new historical data until AFTER I append the historical pull metadata and add the pull_id column with the corresponding value of pull_id to the new historical data
    
  
} else { cat(format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "- No sensors required historical updates.\n") }
}

```

The old workflow for this part of the script:

Retrieve new historical data --> Clean up historical data column names to match database schema --> Append new historical data to Purpleair_air_history --> obtain metadata about historical pull --> Append historical pull metadata to Purpleair_trigger_pulls

The new workflow:

Retrieve new historical data --> Clean up historical data column names to match database schema  --> obtain metadata about historical pull  --> Append historical pull metadata to Purpleair_trigger_pulls --> query newest pull_id from Purpleair_trigger_pulls --> Append new pull_id to new historical data --> Append new historical data to Purpleair_air_history


I then repeated these steps for the Clarity and AirGradient sensors, along with corresponding changes to the update scripts. 

```{r, eval=FALSE}

dbExecute(con, "ALTER TABLE Clarity_air_history ADD pull_id INT")

a<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM Clarity_trigger_pulls")

b<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT pull_id FROM Clarity_air_history")
head(b, 10)

a
```

11/10/26: Downloading historical measurements from EPA sensors using the AirNow R package, which enables data retrieval from the AirNow API

```{r, eval=FALSE}

install.packages("airnow")

```

First, I must instantiate the API key that was randomly generated by the AirNow API Portal when I created a personal account.

```{r}

library(airnow)
set_airnow_key(key="786FD9B7-737A-43E8-8E1D-CDFA43083F67", ask=is_interactive())
get_airnow_key(ask=is_interactive())
get_airnow_key()
```

Test query: retrieving 10 days of historical measurements for EPA sensors in Chicago

```{r, eval=FALSE}

test_historical_data<-get_airnow_monitors(box=c(-87.94009, 41.64458, -87.52509, 42.02295), 
                                      parameters=c("pm25", "ozone", "pm10"),
                                      start_time="2026-11-01T00",
                                      end_time="2026-11-11T00",
                                      monitor_type="both",
                                      data_type="both",
                                      verbose=TRUE,
                                      raw_concentrations=TRUE,
                                      clean_names=TRUE,
                                      api_key = get_airnow_key())


```

The final dataset of historical backfill has 767,963 total observations. However, visual inspection has revealed that not all of these observations are valid. Some observations, especially those in earlier years, contain values of -999.0 for raw and corrected pollutant concentrations, AQI, and AQI category. This is likely a placeholder for NA. 

I investigate how many -999 values exist across all 4 of the aforementioned variables and how many exist for a subset of the variables.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

All_4_variables_NA<-EPA_historical_data%>%
filter(raw_concentration==-999 | value==-999)

sum(EPA_2018_data$raw_concentration==-999 | EPA_2018_data$value==-999 | EPA_2018_data$aqi==-999 | EPA_2018_data$category_number==-999) #59.1% of 2018 observations have at least one of these variables corrupted

sum(EPA_2019_data$raw_concentration==-999 | EPA_2019_data$value==-999 | EPA_2019_data$aqi==-999 | EPA_2019_data$category_number==-999) #36.1% of 2019 observations

sum(EPA_2020_data$raw_concentration==-999 | EPA_2020_data$value==-999 | EPA_2020_data$aqi==-999 | EPA_2020_data$category_number==-999) #2.5% of 2020 observations

sum(EPA_2021_data$raw_concentration==-999 | EPA_2021_data$value==-999 | EPA_2021_data$aqi==-999 | EPA_2021_data$category_number==-999) #1.6% of 2021 observations

sum(EPA_2022_data$raw_concentration==-999 | EPA_2022_data$value==-999 | EPA_2022_data$aqi==-999 | EPA_2022_data$category_number==-999) #2.2% of 2022 observations

sum(EPA_2023_data$raw_concentration==-999 | EPA_2023_data$value==-999 | EPA_2023_data$aqi==-999 | EPA_2023_data$category_number==-999) #1.1% of 2023 observations

sum(EPA_2024_data$raw_concentration==-999 | EPA_2024_data$value==-999 | EPA_2024_data$aqi==-999 | EPA_2024_data$category_number==-999) #1.9% of 2024 observations

sum(EPA_2025_data$raw_concentration==-999 | EPA_2025_data$value==-999 | EPA_2025_data$aqi==-999 | EPA_2025_data$category_number==-999) #0.97% of 2025 observations

sum(EPA_2026_data$raw_concentration==-999 | EPA_2026_data$value==-999 | EPA_2026_data$aqi==-999 | EPA_2026_data$category_number==-999) #1.05% of 2026 observations as of Nov 15

sum(EPA_historical_data$raw_concentration==-999 & EPA_historical_data$value==-999 & EPA_historical_data$aqi == -999 & EPA_historical_data$category_number==-999 )


```

Another useful data exploration is to find the earliest date each sensor reported.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

Earliest_date_by_sensor<-EPA_historical_data%>%
group_by(site_name)%>%
summarize(earliest_timestamp=min(datetime_observed))


```

8 of the 12 sensors began reporting in 2018. The McCook sensor began reporting in December 2023, CHI_MAYFAIR began reporting in November 2024, CHI_WASH began reporting in January 2025, and Summit began reporting in April 2025. 


11/18/26: Adding the EPA historical data and sensor metadata to the database as two new tables

My supervisor advised me to keep rows for which at least one of value or raw_concentration (or both) have a valid measurements, and to not include rows for which both value and raw_concentration are -999. This is very important, as I will include this validation filter when I write the 24 hour update script for the EPA sensors.

```{r, eval=FALSE}


EPA_inv_data<-EPA_historical_data%>%
filter(raw_concentration==-999 & value == -999) 
nrow(EPA_inv_data) #output of 0

```
There are no rows for which both value and raw_concentration take on the null/erroneous value of -999, therefore I will add all the historical data to the database.

First, I must separate the API output into historical data and metadata (like the Airgradient and Clarity sensors, there is no separate metadata endpoint; both metadata nad historical data are in the get_airnow_monitors output)

```{r, eval=FALSE}

colnames(EPA_historical_data)
EPA_historical_readings<-EPA_historical_data%>%
select(site_name, datetime_observed, parameter, unit, raw_concentration, value, aqi, category_number)

EPA_sensor_information<-EPA_historical_data%>%
group_by(site_name)%>%
reframe(latitude=latitude, longitude=longitude, aqs_code=aqs_code, intl_aqs_code=intl_aqs_code, site_agency=site_agency)
EPA_sensor_metadata<-unique.data.frame(EPA_sensor_information) #Keeps only the unique values of each variable, creating a concise metadata table with the 12 sensors

```
Turning -999 values into NA values within the historical dataframe so that someone dosen't accidentally interpret them as valid numeric readings (that is a very easily avoidable way to ruin an entire analysis).

```{r, eval=FALSE}

EPA_historical_readings$raw_concentration=ifelse(EPA_historical_readings$raw_concentration==-999, NA, EPA_historical_readings$raw_concentration)

EPA_historical_readings$value=ifelse(EPA_historical_readings$value==-999, NA, EPA_historical_readings$value)
EPA_historical_readings$aqi=ifelse(EPA_historical_readings$aqi==-999, NA, EPA_historical_readings$aqi)
EPA_historical_readings$category_number=ifelse(EPA_historical_readings$category_number==-999, NA, EPA_historical_readings$category_number)
          



```


Extracting the initial last_seen dates for each sensor (as of 11/15, when I downloaded the historical data):


```{r, eval=FALSE}

last_seen_per_sensor<-EPA_historical_readings%>%
group_by(site_name)%>%
summarize(last_seen=max(datetime_observed))

EPA_sensor_metadata_with_last_seen<-EPA_sensor_metadata%>%
full_join(last_seen_per_sensor, by=c("site_name"="site_name"))

class(EPA_sensor_metadata_with_last_seen$last_seen)

```


Making the historical data and metadata tables (as well as a trigger_pulls table):

```{r, eval=FALSE}

colnames(EPA_sensor_information)

dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE EPA_air_history(
                site_name VARCHAR(50),
                datetime_observed DATETIME NOT NULL,
                parameter VARCHAR(50),
                PRIMARY KEY (site_name, datetime_observed, parameter),  
                unit VARCHAR (50),
                raw_concentration DECIMAL (10, 2),
                value DECIMAL (10, 2),
                aqi INT,
                category_number INT)")

#I need site_name, datetime_observed, AND parameter in the composite primary key because each row of the historical data is its own parameter, opening the possibility of a given site_name/datetime_observed combination mapping to multiple rows (a possiblity this avoids). 

dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE EPA_sensor_information(
                site_name VARCHAR(50) PRIMARY KEY,
                latitude DECIMAL (10, 2),
                longitude DECIMAL (10, 2),
                aqs_code BIGINT,
                intl_aqs_code BIGINT,
                site_agency VARCHAR(50),
                last_seen DATETIME NOT NULL)")


dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE EPA_trigger_pulls(
                pull_id INT IDENTITY (1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
                pull_timestamp DATETIME NOT NULL,
                rows_inserted INT NOT NULL,
                sensors_processed VARCHAR(MAX) NOT NULL)")



```
